title: The tree with its roots above

verses.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचऊर्ध्वमूलमधःशाखमश्वत्थं प्राहुरव्ययम् । छन्दांसि यस्य पर्णानि यस्तं वेद स वेदवित् ॥
verses.tr: The Blessed Lord says: They speak of the imperishable banyan-like tree of the world, with roots above and branches below. The Vedas are its leaves. One who knows this tree knows the Vedas.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna shifts the battlefield into a cosmic vision, asking Arjuna to see the world as an upside-down tree. Hear how the Vedas are described as its leaves.

body.text: The Blessed Lord says: They speak of the imperishable banyan-like tree of the world, with roots above and branches below. The Vedas are its leaves. One who knows this tree knows the Vedas. The word ashvattha points to the world-tree, which has roots above and branches below. The Vedas are its leaves, meaning the deepest knowledge is not in the branches of worldly action but in the roots above. Krishna goes on to explain how this tree grows from the three qualities, tying every living being to the cycle of action and result.

verses.sa: अधश्चोर्ध्वं प्रसृतास्तस्य शाखा     गुणप्रवृद्धा विषयप्रवालाः । अधश्च मूलान्यनुसन्ततानि     कर्मानुबन्धीनि मनुष्यलोके ॥
verses.tr: Its branches spread below, above, and across. They are nourished by the three qualities, with sense-pleasures as their shoots. In the human world, action-bound roots extend everywhere, tying beings to results.
verses.angle: The branches grow below and above, fed by the three gunas
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna now shows how this upside-down tree grows and feeds itself. Listen for the three qualities.

body.text: Its branches spread below, above, and across. They are nourished by the three qualities, with sense-pleasures as their shoots. In the human world, action-bound roots extend everywhere, tying beings to results. The branches of this tree grow below and above, fed by the three qualities. Sense-pleasures act as shoots, while action-bound roots spread everywhere in the human world. Krishna now says that this tree has no true beginning, no end, and no fixed base.

verses.sa: न रूपमस्येह तथोपलभ्यते    नान्तो न चादिर्न च संप्रतिष्ठा । अश्वत्थमेनं सुविरूढमूल    मसङ्गशस्त्रेण दृढेन छित्त्वा ॥
verses.tr: Its form is not perceived here as it truly is: it has no beginning, no end, and no fixed base. Cut down this deeply rooted ashvattha tree with the strong sword of detachment.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: How do you fight a world that has no beginning, no end, and no solid ground? Krishna answers this by naming the weapon and the enemy.

body.text: Its form is not perceived here as it truly is: it has no beginning, no end, and no fixed base. Cut down this deeply rooted ashvattha tree with the strong sword of detachment. Krishna says the form of this world-tree is not perceived as it truly is, and it has no beginning or end. The tree is deeply rooted and must be cut with a strong sword of detachment. Krishna then says to seek that supreme state where one never returns to this cycle.

verses.sa: ततः पदं तत्परिमार्गितव्य    यस्मिन्गता न निवर्तन्ति भूयः । तमेव चाद्यं पुरुषं प्रपद्ये    यतः प्रवृत्तिः प्रसृता पुराणी ॥
verses.tr: Therefore one should seek that supreme state, reaching which one does not return again. I take refuge in that original Person from whom this ancient creation has spread forth.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just described the endless tree of change. Now he points beyond it.

body.text: Therefore one should seek that supreme state, reaching which one does not return again. I take refuge in that original Person from whom this ancient creation has spread forth. The verse names a state, padam, that once reached, stops all return. Krishna then grounds that promise in the original Person, declaring his own refuge in the source from which all of creation spreads. Krishna then lists the qualities of those who reach this imperishable state.

verses.sa: निर्मानमोहा जितसङ्गदोषा    अध्यात्मनित्या विनिवृत्तकामाः । द्वन्द्वैर्विमुक्ताः सुखदुःखसंज्ञै    र्गच्छन्त्यमूढाः पदमव्ययं तत् ॥
verses.tr: Free from pride and delusion, victorious over attachment, ever rooted in the true self, desireless, and beyond the opposites of pleasure and pain, the undeluded reach that imperishable state.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Listen for the pairs of opposites Krishna sets aside. One word names the very things that pull us back and forth.

body.text: Free from pride and delusion, victorious over attachment, ever rooted in the true self, desireless, and beyond the opposites of pleasure and pain, the undeluded reach that imperishable state. Listen to dyvandvaih, from the pairs of opposites. Krishna names the two things that rule ordinary life, pleasure and pain, and says that reaching the highest state means stepping out of their grip. Krishna then says that the sun, moon, and fire do not illumine that place.

verses.sa: न तद्भासयते सूर्यो न शशाङ्को न पावकः । यद्गत्वा न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम ॥
verses.tr: The sun, moon, and fire do not illumine that place. Having reached it, one does not return. That supreme abode is Mine.
verses.angle: Sun, moon and fire do not illumine
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just described the highest reality beyond decay and return. Now he names that goal directly, telling Arjuna about a supreme abode beyond all ordinary light.

body.text: The sun, moon, and fire do not illumine that place. Having reached it, one does not return. That supreme abode is Mine. Three words stand out: sun, moon, and fire. These are the three sources of light in the world, and Krishna says they do not illumine that supreme abode. He then says that anyone who reaches that place does not return to the cycle of birth and death.

verses.sa: ममैवांशो जीवलोके जीवभूतः सनातनः । मनःषष्ठानीन्द्रियाणि प्रकृतिस्थानि कर्षति ॥
verses.tr: The embodied being in this world is my eternal part, yet it draws the mind and the five senses, which rest in nature.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just shown the supreme abode, a place of no return. Now he turns back to the living being still caught in the world, carrying the mind and senses.

body.text: The embodied being in this world is my eternal part, yet it draws the mind and the five senses, which rest in nature. Krishna calls each living being his eternal part, yet the same being draws along the mind and five senses that belong to changing nature. Krishna then shows how this same being carries those senses into a new body, like wind carrying a scent.

verses.sa: शरीरं यदवाप्नोति यच्चाप्युत्क्रामतीश्वरः । गृहीत्वैतानि संयाति वायुर्गन्धानिवाशयात् ॥
verses.tr: Just as the wind carries fragrance from its source, the embodied being carries the mind and senses into a new body.
verses.angle: wind carries fragrance from a source
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: The Gita asks how a person moves from one life to the next. Listen for the exact image that explains what travels.

body.text: Just as the wind carries fragrance from its source, the embodied being carries the mind and senses into a new body. Krishna names one word that moves with the self: the mind. The embodied being leaves one body and enters another, carrying the mind and senses onward, just as wind carries scent from a source. Krishna then shows the inner being using the ears, eyes, skin, tongue, and nose to experience the world.

verses.sa: श्रोत्रं चक्षुः स्पर्शनं च रसनं घ्राणमेव च । अधिष्ठाय मनश्चायं विषयानुपसेवते ॥
verses.tr: Taking hold of the mind, the inner being experiences objects through the ears, eyes, skin, tongue, and nose.
verses.angle: The mind as the base of experience
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna explains how the self moves through the world. Listen for the tool it uses to reach out to objects.

body.text: Taking hold of the mind, the inner being experiences objects through the ears, eyes, skin, tongue, and nose. The verse names five senses, yet it is the mind that takes hold. The senses are only the instruments, and the mind is the hand that reaches out to experience the world. Krishna now explains who is deluded about this process and who truly sees it.

verses.sa: उत्क्रामन्तं स्थितं वापि भुञ्जानं वा गुणान्वितम् । विमूढा नानुपश्यन्ति पश्यन्ति ज्ञानचक्षुषः ॥
verses.tr: The deluded do not see the inner being departing, staying, or enjoying the world through the qualities. Those with the eye of understanding do see.
verses.angle: Who sees and who does not see
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna now asks you to listen for two kinds of sight. One is ordinary sight, and the other is the eye of wisdom. Notice which one sees the truth.

body.text: The deluded do not see the inner being departing, staying, or enjoying the world through the qualities. Those with the eye of understanding do see. Notice who is doing the looking and who is being looked at: the deluded look, but they do not see the self, while those with the eye of knowledge see it. Krishna now turns to the yogis who, with steady practice, are able to see this supreme reality abiding within themselves.

verses.sa: यतन्तो योगिनश्चैनं पश्यन्त्यात्मन्यवस्थितम् । यतन्तोऽप्यकृतात्मानो नैनं पश्यन्त्यचेतसः ॥
verses.tr: The striving yogis see this supreme reality abiding in themselves. The unrefined and thoughtless, even while striving, do not see it.
verses.angle: Effort without refinement is not enough
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna distinguishes between two kinds of people who try, showing that effort without inner refinement is not enough.

body.text: The striving yogis see this supreme reality abiding in themselves. The unrefined and thoughtless, even while striving, do not see it. Listen to the word yatinah, striving, repeated twice. The striving yogis see the supreme reality within, but the thoughtless and unrefined do not, even when they try. Krishna then speaks of the radiance in the sun, moon, and fire that belongs to Him alone.

verses.sa: यदादित्यगतं तेजो जगद्भासयतेऽखिलम् । यच्चन्द्रमसि यच्चाग्नौ तत्तेजो विद्धि मामकम् ॥
verses.tr: The radiance in the sun, the moon, and the fire is Mine alone.
verses.angle: The light of sun, moon and fire
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna moves from the unseen reality to the light that everyone can see.

body.text: The radiance in the sun, the moon, and the fire is Mine alone. Notice the word tejah, radiance, appearing three times. The light that shines in the sun, the moon, and fire is his alone. He then turns from the sky to the earth, sustaining all beings with his power.

verses.sa: गामाविश्य च भूतानि धारयाम्यहमोजसा । पुष्णामि चौषधीः सर्वाः सोमो भूत्वा रसात्मकः ॥
verses.tr: Entering the earth, I sustain all beings with my power. Becoming the moon of life-giving essence, I nourish all plants.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just said the sun, moon, and fire are his alone. Now he explains how he actively sustains the earth and feeds every plant.

body.text: Entering the earth, I sustain all beings with my power. Becoming the moon of life-giving essence, I nourish all plants. He enters the earth itself to support all living beings with his power, and he becomes the moon of life-giving essence to nourish all plants. He now turns from the moon and earth to the fire inside every living being.
